meta.purpose: The editorial layer over the film record. When the Palace corrects a title, moves a film to another category, writes better context, features it, or holds it back, the correction is written here — never by editing the source record and never by letting a YouTube sync overwrite it.
meta.why: Two things must both stay true. The source record is evidence: it says what the archive established and when, and rewriting it in place destroys that. And a later YouTube synchronisation must be able to run repeatedly without undoing anybody's editorial work. Separating the two is what makes both possible — the source stays as it was, this file wins over it, and a sync fills gaps in neither.
meta.precedence: canonical source record  <  these overrides. A sync only ever fills a field that neither has set.

fields.displayTitle: The title shown on the site. Overrides the record's own.
fields.group: One of Palace | Culture | Development | GUDECA | Community | Archive. Overrides the resolver.
fields.category: The fine-grained sourced label shown as a tag and used as a filter.
fields.context: The line of context under the title.
fields.relatedRoute: The Guneku page this film documents.
fields.ordering: Lower sorts earlier. Overrides the record's ordering.
fields.featured: true puts it in the featured position. At most one film should carry this.
fields.highlight: true includes it in the editorial selection shown on the homepage.
fields.state: 'approved' | 'held'. 'held' removes a film from every public surface, immediately and everywhere.

meta.holdRule: Setting state to 'held' is the kill switch. It is honoured by the approval predicate in src/lib/guneku-tv.ts, which every public surface goes through — the watch hub, the homepage, the search index, the sitemap and the structured data. There is no second path to a film that bypasses it.
